title.en: Tourism places (Overture Maps), classified

datasets.note: One row per place. Flood, protected-area, land-use and barrio fields are computed at build time by overlay. The transit-distance fields (transit_m, transit_400m, nearest_stop: the nearest mapped stop of any kind, expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops included) are recomputed by access.py, which the nightly transit refresh also runs. The distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable is in place_access.json. Private homes, holiday rentals, housing, listings named by a street address and care or shelter services are counted but not drawn (places_privacy.py, places_review.json): their rows keep the fields the counts use and carry 'withheld' instead of a name, Overture id, point or nearest stop. No street address, website or other contact detail is published (has_website says only whether one is listed).

review.note: Updated 2026-10-18 under the owner's rule of that date (private residences and listings named by a street address or house number are counted but never drawn or published by name or address; never publish business contact details or any personal data). Done: the street address (28,810 places) and the website (9,683; about 1,240 of them social-media, bio-link or messaging pages, 28 WhatsApp links) are no longer published (has_website keeps the count); a telephone number written into a name is removed (4 names); 1,005 listings (holiday rentals 971 and address-named rented units 34, after the change of the same day below) are counted but not drawn and lose name, Overture id, point, nearest stop and update date, and their confidence is cut down to the map filter's 0.05 step and their distances to a stop to one value per class, and they come last in the file (decision 49) (holiday rentals under the owner's decision of the same day: HANDOFF decision 48, a holiday rental is usually someone's home; hotels, guest houses, inns and B&Bs stay drawn), decided by places_privacy.py with the reviewed list places_review.json (47 public exceptions with reasons, 10 withheld by Overture id only); tests/test_places_privacy.py, check_refresh.py and pages.yml fail on a drawn place that matches a pattern without a review or on a contact field. Still open, so the review stays open on 'name': the names of drawn places are Overture's free text and no rule can tell every person's name from a business name (home-based services under a person's name were withheld by category; others may remain); and, since a second change of 2026-10-18 (HANDOFF decision 47), the listings that are not tourism are left out of the file and of every count: residential buildings, housing estates and subdivisions (2,301), private homes or person-named listings (157), care, shelter and treatment services (52) and numbered homes filed where homes are filed (67), 2,577 in all, 2,370 of them among the 26,579 places counted before. The count on the default basis is now 24,209; the holiday rentals are tourism supply and stay counted. Borderline cases are listed by category in docs/places-privacy.md.

title.en: Global Innovation Index: FPR's 2021 profile of Puerto Rico (GII 2020 method), with updated values and an indicative GII 2026 comparison
title.es: Índice Global de Innovación: el perfil de Puerto Rico de FPR de 2021 (método del GII 2020), con valores actualizados y una comparación indicativa con el GII 2026

datasets.note: 80 indicator records of the Global Innovation Index page of the Knowledge Area (gii.html), which loads it. The 2021 values, ranks 'x / 132' and marks are FPR's profile frozen as printed (docs/analysis/gii-2021/gii_original.json); gii.py adds the newest open value of 16 indicators, all read without an API key (World Bank WGI and WDI, UNESCO UIS, IMF, BLS LAUS and OEWS, US EIA with Census Bureau population; four are FPR estimates with FPR's method) and, for 10 indicators whose source and definition match, Puerto Rico's indicative position among the GII 2026 economies, written X/N, with the 25th, 50th and 75th percentiles (WIPO, CC BY 4.0). Each updated value carries a change marker against the 2021 value in the GII's direction (dir; chg: better, worse, no meaningful change below 5% of the GII 2026 interquartile range, or not comparable) and each indicator its status in the GII 2026 (c26_status: same, renamed, redefined, dropped; docs/analysis/gii-2021/gii_crosswalk.json). No other economy is named or has its values published (a percentile can coincide with one unnamed economy's value), no overall, sub-index or pillar score is computed, and the updated values are not ranked among the GII 2020 economies. FPR's calculation, not an official WIPO ranking. Pillar and indicator texts in English and Spanish are metadata.

review.note: Two questions for Compliance before the 'In review' marker is taken off: (1) the GII 2020 is CC BY-NC-ND 3.0 IGO and FPR's printed ranks place Puerto Rico among its values (a derived result that WIPO can confirm); (2) three 2021 values come from proprietary sources (IHS Markit country risk, Clarivate Web of Science, Brand Finance) and are shown as FPR published them in 2021, with attribution and not updated. The GII 2026 comparison uses WIPO's CC BY 4.0 database and publishes only counts and percentiles, not third-party values.

title.en: Population, age groups, households, veterans, disability, health insurance and schooling by five-year window, 78 municipalities (Census ACS)

datasets.note: The Population domain's first series: 10 variables, four windows (2017-2021 to 2020-2024, labelled by their last year) with margins of error. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). The Census Bureau controls the total population of the island and of 76 municipios to its own estimates and gives it no margin; a share of such a total keeps the margin of its numerator. Built by small_area.py; docs/small-area.md. Since 2026-10-14 (Phase 3 item 9) it also holds the share of people without health insurance (B27010) and of adults 25+ without a high school diploma (B15002), which the barrio and tract files hold too. Since 2026-10-18 it also holds the shares of seven age groups (under 3 and 3 to 4 from B09001, children in households; 5 to 17, 18 to 24, 25 to 44, 45 to 64 and 18 to 44 from B01001): 17 variables; the five-year bands are in population_age.json. Since 2026-10-18 (second step) also the counts of nine age groups (under 3, 3-4, 5-17, 18-24, 25-44, 45-64, 65+, under 18, 18-44), for the municipios only: 26 variables.

title.en: Daytime population and commuting by municipio, calculated from the Census Bureau's commuting flows of 2016-2020 and the 2020 Census
title.es: Población diurna y viajes al trabajo por municipio, calculados con los flujos de viaje al trabajo de 2016-2020 del Negociado del Censo y el Censo 2020

datasets.note: A calculated dataset (decision 107, step 1; commuting.py): the daytime population is the residents of the 2020 Census plus the workers who come in minus the workers who leave, by the Census Bureau's formula for the commuter-adjusted population; the flows are the survey's of 2016-2020, labelled by their last year. Margins of error at 90 percent.

title.en: Public facilities, public school students and main roads inside FEMA's 1% flood area, NOAA's 3 ft sea level rise area and the USGS high landslide susceptibility classes, by municipio (overlaid from the observatory's layers)
title.es: Instalaciones públicas, estudiantes de escuelas públicas y carreteras principales dentro del área de inundación de 1% de FEMA, el área de aumento del nivel del mar de 3 pies de NOAA y las clases de alta susceptibilidad a deslizamientos del USGS, por municipio (superposición de capas del observatorio)

datasets.note: An overlaid dataset (decision 107, step 3; facility_exposure.py): the observatory's facility points, the open public schools of the newest NCES directory and the main roads, laid on FEMA's 1% annual chance flood area, NOAA's 3 ft sea level rise area and the USGS landslide susceptibility map (High or higher; main island only). It says where a building or road stands, not that it floods. Police stations and city halls come from OpenStreetMap (ODbL), so the counts carry its credit.

title.en: Insured bank offices and deposits (2000-2026) and home loans made and denied (2018-2025), by municipio and year (FDIC Summary of Deposits; HMDA)
title.es: Oficinas y depósitos de bancos asegurados (2000-2026) y préstamos hipotecarios otorgados y denegados (2018-2025), por municipio y año (Resumen de Depósitos de la FDIC; HMDA)

datasets.note: Six datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72; decision 107, step 4; credit.py). FDIC: the offices of FDIC-insured banks and the deposits booked at them, June 30 of each year 2000-2026; cooperativas (COSSEC) are not in it. HMDA: home loans made, home purchase loans, their amount and the share of decided applications denied, 2018-2025, counts and sums only; a municipio's amount and denial share have no value under 10 loans or decided applications. No office points: the FDIC places about half the offices at the centre of their ZIP code.

title.en: Drought by municipio and year, 2000-2026 (US Drought Monitor)
title.es: Sequía por municipio y año, 2000-2026 (Monitor de Sequía de EE. UU.)

datasets.note: Three datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72; decision 107, step 5; drought.py), from every weekly map since 2000-01-04: the average share of the area in drought (D1 or worse), and the weeks with drought, and with severe drought (D2 or worse), over half the area. 2026 holds the weeks published so far (to 2026-11-10). Data courtesy of NDMC, via https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu.

title.en: Months for night-time light to come back after Hurricanes María (2017) and Fiona (2022), by municipio
title.es: Meses para que volviera la luz nocturna tras los huracanes María (2017) y Fiona (2022), por municipio

datasets.note: Two datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72; decision 107, step 5, second part; storm_recovery.py), calculated from nightlights_monthly.json with a stated rule: light counts as back when it and the next month are both at least 80% of the same month in the year before the storm (September to August); areas under 0.5 nW/cm²/sr in the year before are too dim to read. The years are the storms: 2017 is María (with Irma earlier that month), 2022 is Fiona. Light is a proxy for power and activity, not a count of homes with power. docs/storm_recovery.md.

title.en: Months for night-time light to come back after Hurricanes María (2017) and Fiona (2022), 901 barrios
title.es: Meses para que volviera la luz nocturna tras los huracanes María (2017) y Fiona (2022), 901 barrios

datasets.note: The same two datasets for the 901 barrios, by the same rule (light counts as back when it and the next month are both at least 80% of the same month in the year before the storm (September to August); areas under 0.5 nW/cm²/sr in the year before are too dim to read). After María 79 barrios, and after Fiona 57, are too dim to read and have no value. storm_recovery.py; docs/storm_recovery.md.

title.en: Road distance to a supermarket, food store, pharmacy, bank or cooperativa, library and fire or EMS station (estimate), by municipio

datasets.note: 7 estimates for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72; decision 107, step 6; essentials.py): the average road distance from where residents live to the nearest place of each kind, each 2020 Census block weighted by its residents, and the share of residents more than 5 km from a supermarket. Shops from Overture places (release 2026-10-21.0) and OpenStreetMap; libraries and fire stations from the map's layers. Only distances are published, never the shops. docs/essentials.md.

title.en: Residents cut off from every hospital when flooded roads or bridges in poor condition close (estimate), by municipio
title.es: Residentes incomunicados de todos los hospitales cuando cierran las carreteras inundables o los puentes en malas condiciones (estimado), por municipio

datasets.note: 5 estimates for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72; decision 107, step 9, third part; cutoff.py): the share of residents with no open road to any hospital when the roads in FEMA's 1% flood area close (with the share of them whose own street is dry), when the bridges in poor condition or closed close, and both, and the residents cut off by floods. A worst case: every flooded road closed at once; expressways and sound bridges stay open. Vieques and Culebra, with no road to a hospital, are left out. docs/cutoff.md.

title.en: Residents cut off from hospitals (estimate), 901 barrios
title.es: Residentes incomunicados de los hospitales (estimado), 901 barrios

datasets.note: The same 5 estimates for the 901 barrios, by the same method (cutoff.py; docs/cutoff.md). A barrio with no residents, and those of Vieques and Culebra, have no value.

title.en: What lies upstream of each reservoir and river gauge: land, residents, buildings, wastewater plants and protected land
title.es: Qué hay aguas arriba de cada embalse y medidor de río: terreno, residentes, edificios, plantas de aguas residuales y terreno protegido

datasets.note: 25 reservoirs and 71 river gauges (decision 107, step 9, fourth part; upstream.py): the land that drains to each, from the NHDPlus HR catchments of What drains here, and the residents, housing units, buildings, wastewater treatment plants in force (EPA POTW, named) and protected land on it. Check: 73 of the 87 sites with a USGS drainage area are within 25% of it. Six off-stream reservoirs have no figures. docs/upstream.md.

title.en: Degrees and certificates awarded by colleges, by level and broad field, by municipio
title.es: Títulos y certificados otorgados por las universidades, por nivel y campo amplio, por municipio

title.en: Public school conditions from the Civil Rights Data Collection (chronic absence, counselors, nurses), by municipio
title.es: Condiciones de las escuelas públicas según la Recopilación de Datos de Derechos Civiles (ausentismo crónico, consejeros, enfermeros), por municipio

title.es: Proveedores de servicios de salud registrados en cada municipio, por tipo (registro NPPES)

title.es: Edad: grupos de cinco años y grupos de edad, conteos y porcentajes por período de cinco años, 78 municipios; grupos amplios de edad para barrios y sectores censales (Censo, ACS)

title.en: Housing, income, work, age and household variables by five-year window, 901 barrios (Census ACS)
title.es: Variables de vivienda, ingresos, trabajo, edad y hogares por período de cinco años, 901 barrios (Censo, ACS)

Every variable also exists for the 78 municipios, under the same key, in housing_series.json, economy_series.json or population_series.json. Over 1 MB, so the medium tier; the Analysis tab reads it only when a person asks for the level. Since 2026-10-18 it also holds the shares of people aged 18 to 44 and 45 to 64 (38 variables): of the age groups, only those whose share is flagged less reliable for under half of the barrios are published below the municipio (docs/small-area.md). The counts of the age groups are municipio only: below the municipio each is flagged for more than half of the barrios (docs/small-area.md section 9).

title.es: Variables de vivienda, ingresos y edad por período de cinco años, 2,555 grupos de bloques (Censo, ACS)

datasets.note: 13 variables for the 2,555 block groups of the 2020 geography: the plan's first wave and three age variables, because the margins are widest here. Tables that the Census Bureau does not publish for block groups (poverty, the Gini index, income by tenure, disability) are not in it. Windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024, labelled by their last year; the estimate and the margin of error (90% confidence) of every area. Every variable also exists for the 78 municipios, under the same key, in housing_series.json, economy_series.json or population_series.json. Built by small_area.py from the ACS tables that acs_small.py reads by byte ranges; method and measured margins: docs/small-area.md. Over 1 MB, so the medium tier; the Analysis tab reads it only when a person asks for the level.

title.en: Public schools and colleges every school year since 2010, by municipio (NCES via the Urban Institute)
title.es: Escuelas públicas y colegios cada año escolar desde 2010, por municipio (NCES mediante el Urban Institute)

datasets.note: Counts for each municipality every school year (a year is the school year that starts in it): public schools open, students, teachers, students per teacher and closures (NCES Common Core of Data), and postsecondary institutions and their fall enrollment (NCES IPEDS), as the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal republishes them under ODC-By 1.0 (credit the Urban Institute and NCES). Never names, addresses, telephone numbers, officers or coordinates. A missing count is no value, never a zero. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). Built by education_series.py; docs/education.md.

title.en: Labor force participation and unemployment of women and men by five-year window, 78 municipalities (Census ACS)
title.es: Participación en la fuerza laboral y desempleo de mujeres y hombres por período de cinco años, 78 municipios (Censo, ACS)

datasets.note: Seven variables for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (key 72, last), each with its 90% margin of error: the labor force participation rate of women 16 and over, of men 16 and over and of women 25 to 54, the gap between men and women in percentage points, the unemployment rate of women, the women 16 and over and the women in the labor force. Three five-year windows that share no year, 2010-2014, 2015-2019 and 2020-2024, labelled 2014, 2019 and 2024, so they can be compared with each other. From ACS table B23001 (sex by age by employment status); participation counts the Armed Forces in the labor force, as table S2301 does; unemployment is over the civilian labor force. Built by women_labor.py with women_labor.json, the file of the Knowledge Area page women-labor.html; the Analysis tab lists the variables under 'Labor force by sex'.

title.en: Women in the labor force: counts by sex and age group with margins of error, for every municipio, the Eastern Region (ERSV) and the tourism regions (Census ACS)
title.es: Las mujeres en la fuerza laboral: conteos por sexo y grupo de edad con márgenes de error, para cada municipio, la Región Este (ERSV) y las regiones turísticas (Censo, ACS)

datasets.note: The data of the Knowledge Area page women-labor.html, which loads it. For Puerto Rico (72) and each of the 78 municipios (keyed by GEOID under areas.<window>), in the three five-year windows that share no year (2010-2014, 2015-2019, 2020-2024; window_ends 2014, 2019, 2024): for each sex and seven age groups (16-19 to 65 and over), the population 16 and over, the labor force (civilian and Armed Forces), the civilian labor force and the unemployed, each as [estimate, 90% margin] (ACS B23001); the women 20 to 64 and those in the labor force by age of own children (B23003); and, for 2020-2024, the survey's unweighted sample of people and housing units (B98003, B98001). groups lists the municipios of the 15-municipio Eastern Region of FPR's Eastern Region Strategic Vision (ERSV, the geography key the contract checks) and of the seven tourism regions, so the page can add counts for any group. analysis holds the page's headline results for the ERSV, computed from these counts: pooled rates (sums of counts, not averages of rates), differences with the rest of the island and their significance at 90%, the age-adjusted rate (direct standardisation to the island's age mix) and its Kitagawa split, and the unweighted mean of the municipio rates for comparison. Built by women_labor.py; method in its docstring and docs/analysis/women-labor-2026-10/README.md.

title.en: Disaster funding and need: FEMA money of 2017 to 2025 and HUD CDBG money of 2019 on by municipio, expected annual loss and residents with three or more risk factors (FEMA, USAspending, Census)
title.es: Fondos por desastres y necesidad: el dinero de FEMA de 2017 a 2025 y el dinero CDBG de HUD desde 2019 por municipio, la pérdida anual esperada y los residentes con tres o más factores de riesgo (FEMA, USAspending, Censo)

datasets.note: The data of the Knowledge Area page public-money.html, which loads it (public_money_need.py; Public money v2, step 5, HANDOFF decision 72). Built only from the observatory's published series, no new source: for each of the 78 municipios (geo.ids), FEMA Public Assistance obligated (money.pa), Individual Assistance approved (money.ia) and Hazard Mitigation federal share approved (money.hma), each summed over the disasters declared or fiscal years 2017 to 2025; the 2020 Census residents (population); FEMA National Risk Index expected annual loss, $ a year (need.eal); Census Community Resilience Estimates, residents with three or more risk factors, % (need.cre3); Hazard Mitigation approved, obligated, awaiting a FEMA decision and approved subapplications (hma). island holds each program's Puerto Rico total, with the money recorded as statewide, and the part placed in the municipios; hma_island the same for Hazard Mitigation. The page divides by residents and cuts each measure into thirds; it states facts and draws no conclusions.

review.note: The FEMA Public Assistance, Individual Assistance and Hazard Mitigation dollars of economy_series.json and housing_series.json, summed by municipio for 2017 to 2025 and set next to two measures of need on a Knowledge Area page. Federal grant content needs Finance and Compliance review before external communication (HANDOFF decisions 9, 21 and 72); no review is recorded. Public data summed over all recipients in each municipio (no recipient is named). The page carries no headline figure and keeps the In review marker and noindex while this review is open. Decision 100 (2026-11-12) adds HUD CDBG-DR, CDBG-MIT and yearly CDBG money read from spending_cdbgdr.json and spending_cdbg.json (USAspending, no license stated, hence licence_class unstated), under the same hold.

summary.en: Finance and Compliance review of federal grant content
summary.es: revisión de Finanzas y Cumplimiento del contenido de fondos federales

title.en: Urban heat: summer surface heat (morning and night) and greenness beside measures of the residents, 901 barrios (Landsat, ECOSTRESS, Sentinel-2, Census)
title.es: Calor urbano: calor de la superficie en verano (mañana y noche) y verdor junto a medidas de los residentes, 901 barrios (Landsat, ECOSTRESS, Sentinel-2, Censo)

datasets.note: The data of the Knowledge Area page urban-heat.html, which loads it (urban_heat.py; terrain and climate plan, step 3, HANDOFF decision 80). Built only from the observatory's published barrio files, no new source: for each of the 901 barrios (geo.ids, the crosswalk's order, with names and municipios), the median summer surface temperature in the morning (land.day, heat_barrio.json) and at night (land.night, night_heat_barrio.json) and the median NDVI (land.ndvi, vegetation_barrio.json); the American Community Survey's latest 5-year shares of residents 65 and older, below poverty, households without a vehicle and living alone, with their margins of error (people, moe; acs_barrio.json); drive time to a general hospital (people.hosp, conditions_barrio.json); the 2020 Census residents (population); and the rank correlations of each pair across the barrios (rho). The page shows the measures side by side, never combined; it states facts and draws no conclusions.

title.en: Medicare enrollment every year since 2013, by municipio (CMS)
title.es: Inscripción en Medicare cada año desde 2013, por municipio (CMS)

datasets.note: People enrolled in Medicare, the share in Medicare Advantage and the share entitled by disability, for each municipio, from CMS's yearly rows (the average of the monthly counts). Counts only. A count CMS suppresses is no value, never a zero. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). Built by medicare_series.py; docs/health.md.

title.en: Hospitals and care facilities, and distance to a health center, by municipio (CMS; observatory estimate from HRSA sites, census blocks and OpenStreetMap roads)
title.es: Hospitales y otras instalaciones de salud, y distancia a un centro de salud, por municipio (CMS; estimado del observatorio con los sitios de HRSA, los bloques censales y las carreteras de OpenStreetMap)

datasets.note: Counts for each municipality of Medicare-certified hospitals, hospitals with an emergency department, dialysis facilities, nursing homes, home health agencies and hospice providers (CMS Provider Data Catalog), and the observatory's estimate of the road distance, drive time and share of residents within 10 km from where residents live (2020 census blocks) to the nearest permanent health center site of HRSA's list, on its OpenStreetMap road graph (care_access.py). The site points stay in the local cache only and are never published (owner decision, 2026-10-14); no names, addresses or certification numbers. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). Built by care_series.py; docs/health.md.

title.en: Drinking water, wastewater, air, hazardous waste, enforcement and toxic release figures, and power plants, by municipio (EPA ECHO, EPA TRI, EIA-860M)
title.es: Cifras de agua potable, aguas usadas, aire, desperdicios peligrosos, cumplimiento y emisiones tóxicas, y plantas de energía, por municipio (EPA ECHO, EPA TRI, EIA-860M)

datasets.note: Counts for each municipality: active community water systems serving it and those with a health-based violation or that are an enforcement priority (EPA ECHO), and operating power plants, generating capacity and renewable capacity (EIA-860M, 2026-09). Since 2026-10-18 also the systems outside PRASA (non-PRASA: privately owned in SDWIS) and the residents they report serving, given to a municipio only when a system serves that one alone. Since 2026-11-11 also the facilities with an individual permit to discharge wastewater (NPDES; EPA ECHO, Clean Water Act), the public sewage treatment plants and major dischargers among them and those with a violation on record, each in the municipality that holds its point. Since 2026-11-11 also the active facilities the Clean Air Act regulates for air pollution (EPA ECHO) and the major sources among them, each in the municipality that holds its point. Since 2026-11-11 also the active handlers of hazardous waste (EPA ECHO, RCRA) and the large quantity generators among them, each in the municipality that holds its point. Since 2026-11-12 also the regulated facilities that were inspected, and those that received a formal enforcement action, in the last five years (EPA ECHO, all programs). Since 2026-11-12 also the pounds of listed toxic chemicals released, in total and to the air, by the facilities that report to the Toxics Release Inventory (reporting year 2024). A water system that serves several municipalities counts in each; Puerto Rico's value counts each system once. No system or facility name is published. Plant points place a plant in a municipality and are never published; no names. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). Built by infrastructure_series.py; docs/infrastructure.md.

title.en: Highway bridges and their condition every year since 2016, by municipio (FHWA National Bridge Inventory)
title.es: Puentes de carretera y su condición cada año desde 2016, por municipio (Inventario Nacional de Puentes de la FHWA)

datasets.note: Bridges, bridges in poor condition (FHWA's rule: the lowest of the deck, superstructure, substructure and culvert ratings is 4 or below) and their share, for each municipality and year. The condition worked out by the rule equals FHWA's own column in every year that has it. Built by infrastructure_series.py; docs/infrastructure.md.

title.en: Natural hazard loss, landslides and wetlands, by municipio (FEMA NRI, USGS, USFWS NWI)
title.es: Pérdida por amenazas naturales, deslizamientos y humedales, por municipio (FEMA NRI, USGS, USFWS NWI)

datasets.note: One value for each municipio, each dataset in its source's year: FEMA's expected annual loss in all and for six hazards (December 2025; an estimate), landslides mapped after Hurricane María (2017) and wetlands and mangroves (almost all mapped from photographs of 1983). FEMA's composite risk score, social vulnerability and resilience are empty for Puerto Rico and are not published. No point or outline is published. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). Built by environment_series.py; docs/environment.md.

title.en: Community resilience (2019-2024) and earthquakes (2000-2025), by municipio (Census CRE, USGS ComCat)
title.es: Resiliencia comunitaria (2019-2024) y terremotos (2000-2025), por municipio (Censo CRE, USGS ComCat)

datasets.note: The shares of residents with no, one or two, and three or more risk factors, with margins (Census Bureau, 2019 and 2021 on; no 2020 release), and earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more and 4.0 or more each year, each placed once in the municipio that holds its epicenter or is nearest offshore (within 25 km of the coast). Built by environment_series.py; docs/environment.md.

title.en: Air and ferry passengers boarding every year, by municipio (BTS T-100, FAA, BTS ferry census)
title.es: Pasajeros que abordan aviones y lanchas cada año, por municipio (BTS T-100, FAA, censo de lanchas de BTS)

datasets.note: Passengers boarding commercial flights (BTS T-100, 2014-2025; FAA enplanements, 2023-2025) and departing flights at the airports of each municipality, and passengers boarding ferries at its terminals (BTS National Census of Ferry Operators: 2019, 2022, 2024). Counts only; no airport or terminal names or points. Cruise passengers are not included: their sources state no license (wanted.json, cruise). Built by gateway_series.py; docs/infrastructure.md.

title.en: Public housing developments (HUD), points
title.es: Residenciales públicos (HUD), puntos

datasets.note: One point per public housing development whose location HUD geocoded to the rooftop or the ZIP+4 centroid (172 of 304 on 2026-10-17), as HUD says to map: name, type (development or scattered site), units, municipio and GEOID. The other developments sit at the centre of a block group or tract in HUD's layer; they are counted in facility_series.json, not drawn. No telephone, e-mail, director or address. The FeatureCollection also carries source, vintage (HUD's date of coverage), notes and built. Built by facilities.py; loaded by the 2D map on first use.

review.note: Public housing is a HUD program. The layer and the counts show where developments are and how many units they hold, no money. Their Spanish was released by the project lead on 2026-10-17 and is recorded in i18n_src/held_for_review.json 'released'.

title.en: Tax credit housing projects (HUD LIHTC), points
title.es: Tax credit housing projects (HUD LIHTC), points

datasets.note: One point per LIHTC project that HUD geocoded to a point in a 2020 census tract (67 of 245 in the 2026-04-30 release): name, type, units, low-income units, year placed in service, municipio and GEOID. The others carry only a city in HUD's database; they are counted in facility_series.json, not drawn. Projects for people who are homeless or living with HIV, and projects whose name says they are a care home (an égida, a "Hogar ..."), are counted, never drawn or named. No address. The FeatureCollection also carries source, vintage, placed_in_service_through, notes and built. Built by facilities.py --only lihtc from the archive saved by hand; loaded by the maps on first use.

review.note: A federal tax credit program (HUD's database of LIHTC projects): the Spanish of its source line, attribution and help text is held (i18n_src/held_for_review.json), as for Table 10 (decision 20). The layer shows where projects are and how many units they hold, no money.

summary.en: Finance and Compliance review of a federal tax credit program's projects (HUD's LIHTC database)
summary.es: revisión de Finanzas y Cumplimiento de los proyectos de un programa federal de crédito contributivo

title.en: Fire and EMS stations (USGS), points
title.es: Estaciones de bomberos y de emergencias médicas (USGS), puntos

datasets.note: Fire and emergency medical service stations of the USGS National Structures Dataset: name, type, municipio (the one that holds the point) and GEOID. No address. The FeatureCollection also carries source, vintage (the newest load date), notes and built. Built by facilities.py; loaded by the 2D map on first use.

title.en: Police stations (OpenStreetMap), points
title.es: Cuarteles de la policía (OpenStreetMap), puntos

datasets.note: Police stations and other police facilities mapped in OpenStreetMap (amenity=police): name (15 have none), type (municipal, state or not stated, read from the name and operator), municipio, GEOID and the OpenStreetMap element id (osm), which lets anyone check or fix the feature. No address, telephone or website. ODbL 1.0: credit OpenStreetMap contributors; a work built on this file shares alike. Built by facilities.py; loaded by the 2D map on first use.

title.en: Public libraries (USAC E-Rate), points
title.es: Bibliotecas públicas (USAC E-Rate), puntos

datasets.note: Active E-Rate libraries that USAC marks as public libraries, drawn where USAC's point falls within 1 km of the municipio of the library's address (1,099 of 1,228 on 2026-11-07): name (any telephone number in it removed), type (main library, library or branch, kiosk, bookmobile), municipio and GEOID. No contact, telephone, e-mail or address. In Puerto Rico the list includes community technology centres registered as public libraries. Built by facilities.py; loaded by the 2D map on first use.

title.en: Public facilities by municipio: public housing, tax credit housing, fire and police stations, libraries
title.es: Instalaciones públicas por municipio: residenciales públicos, vivienda con crédito contributivo, estaciones de bomberos y de policía, bibliotecas

datasets.note: Counts for each municipio and Puerto Rico: public housing developments and units (HUD; every development, drawn or not), LIHTC projects, units and low-income units (HUD's LIHTC database; every project, drawn or not), fire and EMS stations (USGS), police stations (OpenStreetMap, ODbL) and public libraries (USAC E-Rate). Each count has its source's vintage in its ref and in notes.vintages. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). The engine offers them per 1,000 residents (and units per 1,000 housing units). Built by facilities.py.

review.note: Public housing is a HUD program. The layer and the counts show where developments are and how many units they hold, no money. Their Spanish was released by the project lead on 2026-10-17 and is recorded in i18n_src/held_for_review.json 'released'.

A federal tax credit program: the Spanish labels of the three LIHTC counts are held (i18n_src/held_for_review.json) and their dictionary entries have no Spanish summary until Finance and Compliance review them (decisions 20 and 21).

summary.en: Finance and Compliance review of the tax credit housing counts (HUD's LIHTC database)
summary.es: revisión de Finanzas y Cumplimiento de los conteos de vivienda con crédito contributivo

title.en: Tax-exempt organizations by municipio and NTEE major group (IRS)
title.es: Organizaciones exentas de contribuciones por municipio y grupo principal NTEE (IRS)

datasets.note: Counts only, for each municipio and Puerto Rico: organizations in the IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File with a Puerto Rico address, in all, 501(c)(3) and in the ten NTEE major groups (Z and no code together). No name, EIN or address is published or kept in the cache. An organization is counted at its headquarters address (city, else ZIP code). Puerto Rico's value counts every organization in the file. Built by nonprofits.py.

title.en: Local conditions by municipio: EPA-regulated sites, impaired waters, non-attainment areas, severe housing problems (HUD CHAS), street intersections and drive time to a general hospital
title.es: Condiciones locales por municipio: instalaciones reguladas por la EPA, aguas deterioradas, zonas de incumplimiento, problemas graves de vivienda (HUD CHAS), intersecciones de calles y tiempo en auto a un hospital general

datasets.note: 14 datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72), each in its source's vintage (TRI reporting year 2024; FRS, Green Book and CMS read 2026-10-17; ATTAINS cycle 2024; LMOP data of 2024-09; CHAS 2016-2020; TIGER/Line 2026): counts of TRI facilities, active RMP facilities, Superfund NPL sites and LMOP landfills (open or closed, and open); the share of the area inside a 303(d)-listed assessment unit and inside a lead or sulfur dioxide non-attainment area; households with severe housing problems and their share (exact sums of HUD CHAS tracts); street intersections and their density per square mile (TIGER/Line); the observatory's estimate of the drive time and road distance to the nearest general hospital, averaged over each municipio's barrios by residents (no value for Vieques and Culebra). Each variable names its barrio file (barrioFile). No names, addresses or points of sites or hospitals are published. The class is the strictest of the sources: OpenStreetMap (roads, hospital buildings) is ODbL. Built by conditions.py; docs/conditions.md.

review.note: HUD CHAS is HUD's planning data (households with severe housing problems), not grant money. Its Spanish (labels, titles, summaries) was released by the project lead on 2026-10-17 and is recorded in i18n_src/held_for_review.json 'released'.

title.en: Local conditions by barrio: EPA-regulated sites, impaired waters, non-attainment areas, severe housing problems (HUD CHAS, estimated), street intersections and drive time to a general hospital, 901 barrios
title.es: Condiciones locales por barrio: instalaciones reguladas por la EPA, aguas deterioradas, zonas de incumplimiento, problemas graves de vivienda (HUD CHAS, estimados), intersecciones de calles y tiempo en auto a un hospital general, 901 barrios

datasets.note: The same 14 datasets as conditions_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's), with no value for Puerto Rico. Sites are counted in the barrio that holds their point; area shares are measured on the barrio outlines of barrios.geojson; the severe housing problems are ESTIMATES spread from census tracts by 2020 housing units (docs/geography.md, section 4); the drive time is from the barrio's population-weighted point, 0 when the barrio holds a hospital, and empty where no road reaches a hospital (Vieques, Culebra, Isla de Mona, one uninhabited barrio of Utuado). The Analysis tab reads it the first time a layer of these datasets is shaded by barrio. Built by conditions.py; docs/conditions.md.

review.note: As for conditions_series.json: the Spanish that names HUD (the CHAS labels, this file's title, the dictionary summaries) was released by the project lead on 2026-10-17.

title.en: Historic places on the National Register (NPS), points
title.es: Lugares en el Registro Nacional de Lugares Históricos (NPS), puntos

datasets.note: Listings of Puerto Rico on the National Register of Historic Places as the National Park Service's public locations service maps them: name, type (historic building, structure, district, site or object), municipio, GEOID and listing date (listed, YYYY-MM or YYYY-MM-DD). One point per listing and municipio: a listing with points in several municipios (a historic road, an irrigation system) has one in each. Listings with only an outline are placed at a point inside it. Private residences, and listings whose name holds a street address or house number, are not drawn (counted in community_series.json; notes.counted_not_drawn and notes.counted_not_drawn_by_municipio give how many). No address. Built by community_assets.py; loaded by the 2D map on first use.

review.note: Cleared on 2026-10-18: decided by FPR to treat the National Register's public spatial data as a US Government work in the public domain, as other federal data are (sources.json: nps_nrhp). NPS states no named licence; the map service's licence field says 'For general public distribution' and the metadata says the public data are provided as general reference data.

Cleared on 2026-10-18: decided by FPR that private homes are counted but not drawn. community_assets.py counts every listing in its municipio (nrhp_places) and draws only the others: a listing reviewed as a private residence, or whose name holds a street address or house number, gets no point and its name is published nowhere. NPS gives no ownership or use field, so name patterns (Casa, House, Residencia, Residence, Home, Villa, Chalet, Quinta, Hacienda, a number or a street word) pick the listings to review, and nrhp_review.json holds each decision with its reason; a listing that matches and is not reviewed is counted only. On 2026-10-18: 72 of 342 listings counted only (7 of them named by a street address or house number, 10 haciendas), 270 drawn, among them 43 that match a pattern and are public buildings, museums, public heritage sites or numbered bridges, roads and lodges. tests/test_community.py checks that no drawn point is an unreviewed residence and that no residence's name is in a generated file.

title.en: City halls (OpenStreetMap), points
title.es: Alcaldías (OpenStreetMap), puntos

datasets.note: City halls (alcaldías) mapped in OpenStreetMap (amenity=townhall): name (3 have none), type (city hall or city hall annex), municipio, GEOID and the OpenStreetMap element id (osm). 65 features in 62 municipios on 2026-10-18; notes.municipios_without_a_city_hall_mapped lists the 16 municipios with none mapped. No address, telephone or website. ODbL 1.0: credit OpenStreetMap contributors; a work built on this file shares alike. Built by community_assets.py (refreshed by hand); loaded by the 2D map on first use.

title.en: Historic places and treatment facilities by municipio (NPS, SAMHSA)
title.es: Lugares históricos y centros de tratamiento por municipio (NPS, SAMHSA)

datasets.note: Counts for each municipio and Puerto Rico: places on the National Register of Historic Places (NPS; every listing, private residences included; a listing with points in several municipios counts in each, Puerto Rico counts it once) and substance use and mental health treatment facilities from SAMHSA's 2025 National Directories (survey of 2024), in all and by type of care (substance use only, mental health only, both). Treatment facilities are counts only: no name, address or point is kept or published. The key list includes 72 (Puerto Rico as a whole). The engine offers them per 1,000 residents. Built by community_assets.py; docs/community.md.

title.en: Landslide susceptibility by municipio: land in each class, and land and residents in the high, very high and extremely high classes (USGS, Hughes and Schulz 2020)
title.es: Susceptibilidad a deslizamientos por municipio: terreno en cada clase, y terreno y residentes en las clases alta, muy alta y extremadamente alta (USGS, Hughes y Schulz 2020)

datasets.note: 9 datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72), from the USGS map of susceptibility to landslides triggered by intense rainfall (5 m, main island only; published 2020, GIS layer 2021): the share of the land in the high-or-above and very-high-or-above classes, and the 2020 census residents (count and share) whose block's internal point lies in the high-or-above classes (an estimate), and the share of the land in each of the five classes (one dataset each, since 2026-10-18). Vieques and Culebra are not in the map and have no value; Puerto Rico's figures are the main island's. Read from the first author's tile copy of the raster (ScienceBase refuses scripts) and checked against the report's class areas and table 5. Each variable names its barrio file (barrioFile). Built by landslide.py; docs/landslide.md.

title.en: Landslide susceptibility by barrio: land in each class, and land and residents in the high, very high and extremely high classes, 901 barrios (USGS, Hughes and Schulz 2020)
title.es: Susceptibilidad a deslizamientos por barrio: terreno en cada clase, y terreno y residentes en las clases alta, muy alta y extremadamente alta, 901 barrios (USGS, Hughes y Schulz 2020)

datasets.note: The same 9 datasets as landslide_series.json for the 901 barrios (the share of the land in the high classes and in each of the five classes, and the residents in the high classes), under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's). Land shares are measured on the barrio outlines of barrios.geojson from the map read at about 4.5 m a pixel; residents count whole 2020 census blocks by their internal point (an estimate, rough for a barrio). Empty for the barrios of Vieques, Culebra and Isla de Mona, which the map does not cover. The Analysis tab reads it the first time a layer of these datasets is shaded by barrio. Built by landslide.py; docs/landslide.md.

title.en: Surface heat by municipio: daytime land surface temperature on clear summer mornings, and land and residents among Puerto Rico's hottest tenth (Landsat 8 and 9)
title.es: Calor de superficie por municipio: temperatura diurna de la superficie terrestre en mañanas despejadas de verano, y terreno y residentes entre la décima parte más caliente de Puerto Rico (Landsat 8 y 9)

datasets.note: 5 datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72), from USGS Landsat 8 and 9 Collection 2 Level-2 surface temperature, June to September of the last three complete summers: the median and 90th percentile of a clear-sky composite at 60 m (mid-morning, about 10:30 local time), the share of land above Puerto Rico's 90th percentile, and the 2020 census residents (count and share) whose block's internal point lies on that land (an estimate). Surface temperature, not air temperature. Municipios and Puerto Rico pool the cells of their barrios. Each variable names its barrio file (barrioFile). Built by heat.py with raster.py; docs/heat.md.

title.es: Calor de superficie por barrio: temperatura diurna de la superficie terrestre en mañanas despejadas de verano, y terreno y residentes entre la décima parte más caliente de Puerto Rico, 901 barrios (Landsat 8 y 9)

title.en: Surface heat image: median land surface temperature of clear summer mornings, 60 m cells, as one Web Mercator picture (Landsat 8 and 9)
title.es: Imagen del calor de la superficie: temperatura mediana de la superficie terrestre en mañanas despejadas de verano, celdas de 60 m, en una sola imagen Web Mercator (Landsat 8 y 9)

datasets.note: The 60 m composite of heat.py drawn as an indexed PNG (64 colour steps of a blue-grey-red scale around Puerto Rico's median; transparent where there is no value). About one cell per pixel, Web Mercator, under 4,096 pixels wide. Mona, Monito and Desecheo are left out. Its corners and scale are in heat_surface.json. The 2D map and the 3D view draw it when its switch is on. Built by heat.py with surface_image.py; docs/heat.md. Over 1 MB, so the medium tier.

datasets.note: The corners (west, south, east, north), size, pixel size and colour scale (low, centre and high in °C, steps and colour stops) of heat_surface.png, with the window and source of the composite. Built by heat.py; docs/heat.md.

title.es: Imagen del calor de la superficie de noche: sus esquinas, su tamaño y su escala de color

datasets.note: The corners, size, pixel size and colour scale of night_heat_surface.png, with the window and source of the night composite. Built by ecostress.py; docs/ecostress.md.

Municipios and Puerto Rico pool the cells of their barrios. Each variable names its barrio file (barrioFile). Built by vegetation.py with raster.py; docs/vegetation.md.

title.en: Vegetation by barrio: greenness (NDVI) on clear summer days, land with dense vegetation and with little or none, and residents on land with little or none, 901 barrios (Sentinel-2)
title.es: Vegetación por barrio: verdor (NDVI) en días despejados de verano, terreno con vegetación densa y con poca o ninguna, y residentes en terreno con poca o ninguna, 901 barrios (Sentinel-2)

datasets.note: The same 5 datasets as vegetation_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's). title.en: Buildings by municipio: counts, buildings per km², land under roofs, median footprint, buildings in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area and the share traced by machine learning (Overture)
title.es: Edificios por municipio: conteos, edificios por km², terreno bajo techo, huella mediana, edificios en un Área Especial de Riesgo de Inundación de FEMA y la proporción trazada con aprendizaje automático (Overture)

datasets.note: 7 datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72), from the Overture Maps buildings theme (OpenStreetMap, Google Open Buildings and Microsoft ML Buildings footprints): the number of buildings, buildings per km² of Census land, the footprints' share of the land, the median footprint in m² on an equal-area plane, the buildings whose inner point is in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area of flood.geojson (count and share), and the share not from OpenStreetMap. Municipios and Puerto Rico pool their barrios. No building is published one by one. A derived database of ODbL data, offered under ODbL 1.0. Each variable names its barrio file (barrioFile). Built by buildings.py; docs/buildings.md.

title.en: Buildings by barrio: counts, buildings per km², land under roofs, median footprint, buildings in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area and the share traced by machine learning, 901 barrios (Overture)
title.es: Edificios por barrio: conteos, edificios por km², terreno bajo techo, huella mediana, edificios en un Área Especial de Riesgo de Inundación de FEMA y la proporción trazada con aprendizaje automático, 901 barrios (Overture)

datasets.note: The same 7 datasets as buildings_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's). A building belongs to the barrio whose outline (barrios.geojson) holds a point inside its footprint, or the nearest within 100 m. A derived database of ODbL data, offered under ODbL 1.0. The Analysis tab reads it the first time a layer of these datasets is shaded by barrio. Built by buildings.py; docs/buildings.md.

title.en: Buildings missing from the base map, for the 3D view: footprints and heights from Google and Microsoft that OpenStreetMap does not have (Overture)
title.es: Edificios que faltan en el mapa base, para la vista 3D: huellas y alturas de Google y Microsoft que OpenStreetMap no tiene (Overture)

datasets.note: A PMTiles file of vector tiles (layer b, zooms 13 and 14) with the building footprints in Overture's buildings theme whose geometry source is not OpenStreetMap, and each one's height and base height when Overture has them; nothing else (no id, name, class or source record). The 3D view draws it under the "3D buildings" switch beside the base map's buildings. A derived database of ODbL data, offered under ODbL 1.0. Built by buildings3d.py; docs/buildings3d.md.

title.en: Vegetation fire detections from satellite by municipio: each year since 2019, per 100 km² of land, and the last 12 months (NASA FIRMS, NOAA-20)
title.es: Detecciones de fuegos de vegetación por satélite por municipio: cada año desde 2019, por 100 km² de terreno y los últimos 12 meses (NASA FIRMS, NOAA-20)

datasets.note: Counts for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72) of VIIRS 375 m active fire detections on NOAA-20 that FIRMS tags as presumed vegetation fires (type 0) with nominal or high confidence: each complete year from 2019 (yearly country files, no key) and the last 12 months (area API with the FIRMS_MAP_KEY secret; near-real-time detections near a static land source left out). A detection belongs to the municipio of the barrio that holds its pixel's centre. No point is published. Built by fires.py in GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/fires.yml, refresh unit fires); docs/fires.md.

title.en: Night surface heat by municipio: land surface temperature on clear summer nights, and land and residents among Puerto Rico's warmest tenth at night (NASA ECOSTRESS)
title.es: Calor de superficie de noche por municipio: temperatura de la superficie terrestre en noches despejadas de verano, y terreno y residentes entre la décima parte más cálida de Puerto Rico de noche (NASA ECOSTRESS)

datasets.note: 5 datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72), from NASA ECOSTRESS ECO_L2T_LSTE version 2 (70 m), the night passes between 21:00 and 06:00 of June to September of the last three complete summers (the window of heat_series.json): the median and 90th percentile of a clear-sky night composite on heat.py's 60 m grid, the share of land above Puerto Rico's night 90th percentile, and the 2020 census residents (count and share) whose block's internal point lies on that land (an estimate). Surface temperature, not air temperature. Municipios and Puerto Rico pool the cells of their barrios. Built by ecostress.py with raster.py, in GitHub Actions with the NASA Earthdata token; docs/ecostress.md.

title.en: Night surface heat by barrio: land surface temperature on clear summer nights, and land and residents among Puerto Rico's warmest tenth at night, 901 barrios (NASA ECOSTRESS)
title.es: Calor de superficie de noche por barrio: temperatura de la superficie terrestre en noches despejadas de verano, y terreno y residentes entre la décima parte más cálida de Puerto Rico de noche, 901 barrios (NASA ECOSTRESS)

datasets.note: The same 5 datasets as night_heat_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's). A 60 m cell belongs to the barrio whose outline (barrios.geojson) holds its centre; residents count whole 2020 census blocks by their internal point (an estimate, rough for a barrio). The Analysis tab reads it the first time a layer of these datasets is shaded by barrio. Built by ecostress.py; docs/ecostress.md.

title.en: Climb on the walk to a transit stop by municipio: round-trip climb and walks with a stretch steeper than a ramp may be (USGS 3DEP)
title.es: Subida en el camino a una parada de transporte por municipio: subida de ida y vuelta y caminos con un tramo más empinado de lo que puede ser una rampa (USGS 3DEP)

datasets.note: 3 datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72): for the residents within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable (the walkers of walk_cur in the exposure files, on their as_of date), the residents-weighted median round-trip climb of the walk along the mapped roads, and the residents (share and count) whose walk has a 30 m stretch steeper than 1 in 12, the steepest running slope of a ramp under the 2010 ADA Standards; heights from USGS 3DEP 1/3 arc-second, every 10 m. An area with no walkers has no value. Built by climb.py with walknet.py and raster.py; docs/climb.md.

title.en: Climb on the walk to a transit stop by barrio, 901 barrios (USGS 3DEP)
title.es: Subida en el camino a una parada de transporte por barrio, 901 barrios (USGS 3DEP)

datasets.note: The same 3 datasets as climb_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's). A block counts whole in the barrio the crosswalk gives it. Built by climb.py; docs/climb.md.

title.en: Reservoir levels (USGS), points
title.es: Niveles de los embalses (USGS), puntos

datasets.note: One point per reservoir with a live USGS gauge (25, 19 in AAA's daily report): name, type, municipio, GEOID, USGS monitoring location, whether AAA reports it, the latest level at build time, 120 daily levels and the usual level of each week (10th to 90th percentile of 2011-2025). The page replaces the latest level with a live reading from USGS when the layer is switched on. AAA's alert levels are not included (no licence stated). The FeatureCollection also carries source, vintage, built and notes. Built by reservoirs.py; loaded by the maps on first use.

title.en: River flow (USGS), points
title.es: Caudal de los ríos (USGS), puntos

datasets.note: One point per river or stream with a live USGS gauge (71 gauges on 54 rivers and streams on 2026-11-11): the river's name, type, municipio, GEOID, USGS monitoring location, the name USGS gives the gauge, the latest flow at build time, 120 daily flows and the usual flow of each week (10th to 90th percentile of 2011-2025), in cubic metres per second. The page replaces the latest flow with a live reading from USGS when the layer is switched on. No flood stage is included: a flow higher than usual is not a flood warning. The FeatureCollection also carries source, vintage, built and notes. Built by river_gauges.py; loaded by the maps on first use. Since 2026-11-12 also each gauge's height of water (metres on the gauge's own scale) and, for 1 gauge, the flood reference levels USGS has surveyed (USGS Real-Time Flood Impacts). Since 2026-11-12 also, for 66 gauges, nws: the flood stages the National Weather Service has set there (action, minor, moderate, major), in metres of gauge height.

title.en: Groundwater levels (USGS), points
title.es: Niveles del agua subterránea (USGS), puntos

datasets.note: One point per well with a live USGS gauge (34 wells in 24 municipios on 2026-11-12): the well's name, type, municipio, GEOID, USGS monitoring location, the name USGS gives the well, the latest depth to water at build time, how deep the well was built (where USGS records it), 120 daily depths and the usual depth of each week (10th to 90th percentile of 2011-2025), in metres below the ground. The page replaces the latest depth with a live reading from USGS when the layer is switched on. A well shows one point of one aquifer; the file says nothing about water quality. The FeatureCollection also carries source, vintage, built and notes. Built by groundwater.py; loaded by the maps on first use.

title.en: Rainfall (USGS rain gauges), points
title.es: Lluvia (pluviómetros de USGS), puntos

datasets.note: One point per USGS rain gauge that is reporting now (54 gauges in 30 municipios on 2026-11-12): the gauge's name, type, municipio, GEOID, USGS monitoring location, the name USGS gives the site, 120 daily rain totals and the usual rain of each week (10th to 90th percentile of 2011-2025), in millimetres. The page reads the rain of the last 24 hours and the last 7 days from USGS when the layer is switched on. A gauge measures one spot; the file is not a flood warning or a forecast. The FeatureCollection also carries source, vintage, built and notes. Built by rain_gauges.py; loaded by the maps on first use.

title.en: Power plants (EIA-860M), points
title.es: Plantas de energía (EIA-860M), puntos

datasets.note: One point per power plant in EIA-860M's Puerto Rico sheets (67 plants with an operating generator in 40 municipios and 1 planned plant, file of September 2026): the plant's name as EIA writes it, type, municipio, GEOID, EIA plant id, main technology, operating nameplate MW without batteries, battery MW and MWh, MW by technology, MW on standby and out of service, operating generators, first and last operating year, MW planned and the earliest expected month, and status. Owner names are never kept (HANDOFF decision 104 (b)).

title.en: Transmission lines (OpenStreetMap), lines
title.es: Líneas de transmisión (OpenStreetMap), líneas

datasets.note: OpenStreetMap's power lines and cables of 230, 115 and 38 kV (752, 900 and 1,052 km on 2026-11-14), joined by voltage and simplified to about 100 m; the 549 substations are counted by municipio in the notes, never drawn. No name, operator or circuit number (HANDOFF decision 104 (c)). ODbL.

title.en: Energy in Puerto Rico (Knowledge Area data)
title.es: Energía en Puerto Rico (datos del Área de conocimiento)

datasets.note: Production by source every month since 2010, rooftop solar customers and capacity, batteries, electricity sales and smart meters by municipio, rooftop solar by LUMA district, SAIDI, the residential price against the United States and the transmission lines and plants inside FEMA flood hazard areas (HANDOFF decision 104, step 3). LUMA's filings state no licence.

title.en: Energy by municipio: home and business batteries, electricity sales, smart meters (LUMA) and households paying $250 or more a month for electricity (ACS)
title.es: Energía por municipio: baterías en hogares y negocios, ventas de electricidad, contadores inteligentes (LUMA) y hogares que pagan $250 o más al mes de electricidad (ACS)

datasets.note: The Explore and Analysis datasets of decision 104, step 4 (energy_municipios.py): battery installations and their MWh and the smart-meter share at the end of each year (the current year at the latest month), electricity sales by calendar year (LUMA's monthly metrics filed with the Energy Bureau), and the households paying $250 or more a month for electricity with margins of error (ACS 5-year B25132). San Juan adds LUMA's San Juan, Río Piedras and Santurce areas.

title.en: Households paying $250 or more a month for electricity, by barrio (ACS 5-year B25132)
title.es: Hogares que pagan $250 o más al mes de electricidad, por barrio (ACS quinquenal B25132)

datasets.note: The barrio values of en_bill250_pct and en_bill250_n (energy_municipios.py), windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024, with margins of error.

title.en: Wastewater, air and hazardous waste facilities by barrio, 901 barrios (EPA ECHO)
title.es: Instalaciones de aguas usadas, aire y desperdicios peligrosos por barrio, 901 barrios (EPA ECHO)

datasets.note: Seven of the counts of infrastructure_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's): facilities with a wastewater discharge permit, public sewage treatment plants, major wastewater dischargers, air pollution sources, major air sources, hazardous waste handlers and large generators. A facility counts in the barrio whose outline holds its point, or the nearest outline within 2 km. Counts only: no name, address or point. The counts of violations, inspections and enforcement actions and the pounds of toxic releases are not given by barrio. Built by infrastructure_series.py; docs/infrastructure.md.

title.en: Night-time light by municipio and year, 2012-2025: mean radiance and the share of pixels of poor quality (NASA Black Marble VNP46A3)
title.es: Luz nocturna por municipio y año, 2012-2025: radiancia media y proporción de píxeles de calidad baja (NASA Black Marble VNP46A3)

datasets.note: Two datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72), for each complete calendar year 2012-2025: the mean night-time radiance (nW/cm²/sr) of the 15 arc-second pixels whose centre lies in the area, pooled over the year's twelve monthly composites, and the share of those pixels flagged poor quality or gap-filled. A municipio's and Puerto Rico's figures pool all their pixels, not barrio means. A proxy for activity and electric power, not a count. Read with a free NASA Earthdata login used only by the build (HANDOFF decision 75). Built by nightlights.py; docs/nightlights.md.

title.en: Night-time light by barrio and year, 2012-2025, 901 barrios (NASA Black Marble VNP46A3)
title.es: Luz nocturna por barrio y año, 2012-2025, 901 barrios (NASA Black Marble VNP46A3)

datasets.note: The same two datasets as nightlights_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's). A pixel is about 460 m across, so a small barrio rests on few pixels; the three barrios smaller than a pixel take the pixel under them. The Analysis tab reads it the first time a layer of these datasets is shaded by barrio. Built by nightlights.py; docs/nightlights.md.

title.en: Night-time light by month, 2012-01 to 2026-09, for the 78 municipios, Puerto Rico and the 901 barrios (NASA Black Marble VNP46A3)
title.es: Luz nocturna por mes, de 2012-01 a 2026-09, para los 78 municipios, Puerto Rico y los 901 barrios (NASA Black Marble VNP46A3)

datasets.note: One value for each area and month: the mean radiance and the quality share of the monthly composite, for the municipios and Puerto Rico (municipio.ids) and the barrios (barrio.ids). No page reads it yet; it is for time-series charts. Built by nightlights.py; docs/nightlights.md.

title.en: Fixed broadband by municipio, June 2023-2026: locations, the shares served, underserved and unserved (NTIA BEAD tiers), and fiber (FCC Broadband Data Collection)
title.es: Banda ancha fija por municipio, junio de 2023 a 2026: ubicaciones, proporciones servidas, subatendidas y sin servicio (niveles BEAD de la NTIA) y fibra (FCC, Broadband Data Collection)

datasets.note: Six datasets for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (the key list ends with 72), for the FCC's release as of June 30 of each year 2023-2026: broadband serviceable locations, the shares served (100/20 Mbps or more), underserved (25/3 to 100/20) and unserved (below 25/3) by the best low-latency service over a reliable technology (NTIA BEAD), the locations below 100/20, and the share where fiber is available. Counts by census block, summed by area; no location, address or provider is published. Read with FPR's FCC account in GitHub Actions (secrets FCC_BDC_USERNAME and FCC_BDC_HASH). Built by broadband.py; docs/broadband.md.

title.en: Fixed broadband by barrio, June 2023-2026, 901 barrios (FCC Broadband Data Collection)
title.es: Banda ancha fija por barrio, junio de 2023 a 2026, 901 barrios (FCC, Broadband Data Collection)

datasets.note: The same six datasets as broadband_series.json for the 901 barrios, under the same keys, in the order of geo.ids (the crosswalk's). Each census block is placed in its barrio by its internal point; the barrios add up exactly to the municipios. A barrio with no location has no share. The Analysis tab reads it the first time a layer of these datasets is shaded by barrio. Built by broadband.py; docs/broadband.md.

title.en: Broadband gaps by H3 hexagon, newest June release (FCC Broadband Data Collection), map layer
title.es: Brechas de banda ancha por hexágono H3, publicación de junio más reciente (FCC, Broadband Data Collection), capa del mapa

datasets.note: One hexagon per H3 resolution-8 cell with 10 or more broadband serviceable locations in the FCC's newest June release: the cell id (h), locations (n), the shares below 100/20 Mbps, unserved and with fiber, and the municipio that holds most of its locations (mun). Cells with fewer locations are counted in notes, not drawn. Built by broadband.py with FPR's FCC account in GitHub Actions; drawn by the 2D map and the 3D view from core/facilities.js on first use (decision 101). Tier medium on purpose: about 10,000 hexagons are 2.9 MB raw but about 330 KB compressed, and the maps load the file only when the layer is switched on.

title.en: Residents, housing units, buildings and residents in the flood area, by hexagon of 1 km² (map layer)
title.es: Residentes, unidades de vivienda, edificios y residentes en el área de inundación, por hexágono de 1 km² (capa del mapa)

datasets.note: One equal-area hexagon of 1 km² for each cell with a resident, a housing unit or a building (8,745 cells; decision 107, step 9, first part; hexgrid.py): residents (p) and housing units (h) from the 2020 Census blocks counted whole by their internal point, buildings (b) and land under buildings (bf, %) from Overture's footprints, and residents in FEMA's 1% flood area (pf, %). The cells add up exactly to the island's residents, housing units and buildings. Tier medium on purpose: 2.4 MB raw, about 330 KB compressed, loaded when the layer is switched on.

title.en: Opportunity Zones 2.0: the status of every 2020 census tract (zone, rural or not; eligible; not eligible), residents in zones by barrio and municipio, and the first round (US Treasury)
title.es: Zonas de Oportunidad 2.0: el estado de cada sector censal de 2020 (zona, rural o no; elegible; no elegible), los residentes en zonas por barrio y municipio, y la primera ronda (Tesoro de EE. UU.)

datasets.note: The data of the Knowledge Area page opportunity-zones.html (HANDOFF decision 103). tracts: the 981 tracts of 2020 (tract_fields: id, municipio, tract number, status 2 zone rural / 1 zone not rural / 0 eligible not designated / -1 not eligible, Treasury's rural flag, poverty rate, median family income and its percent of the comparison area's (ACS 2020-2024, as Treasury published them), the comparison area (an index of areas), 2020 Census residents and housing units, land km², the barrios with residents in the tract); barrios: 2020 residents, residents in zones and in eligible tracts (blocks counted whole); municipios: tracts, eligible, zones, rural zones, residents and land in zones; pr: Puerto Rico's totals, the 25 percent limit; groups: medians by status; first_round: the 2018 zones (2010 tracts) and their 2010 residents. Designated 2026-11-05 for 2027-01-01 to 2036-12-31. Built by opportunity_zones.py; docs/opportunity-zones.md.

title.en: Opportunity Zones 2.0: the designated census tracts, rural or not (US Treasury), map layer
title.es: Zonas de Oportunidad 2.0: los sectores censales designados, rurales o no (Tesoro de EE. UU.), capa del mapa

datasets.note: One polygon per designated tract (178): g (tract GEOID), c (2 rural, 1 not rural), m (municipio), t (tract number), p (2020 Census residents), pv (poverty rate) and mr (median family income as a percent of the area's, ACS 2020-2024 as Treasury published them), b (up to three barrios with the most residents in the tract) and nb (barrios with residents). Outlines of the Census Bureau's 1:500,000 cartographic file, to 4 decimals: for drawing only. Drawn by the 2D map and the 3D view from core/facilities.js on first use (layer oz). Built by opportunity_zones.py.

title.en: Commonwealth budget: spent, approved and proposed by agency, fund, function and concept of expense (OGP)
title.es: Presupuesto del Gobierno de Puerto Rico: gastado, aprobado y propuesto por agencia, fondo, función y concepto de gasto (OGP)

datasets.note: Public spending PR 3 (ogp_budget.py, HANDOFF decision 77). The agencies in the fiscal plan, island-wide (the budget names no municipio). columns: one per fiscal year (July to June, named by the year it ends) and stage (actual = Gastado, approved, proposed), each from the newest data sheet whose lines add up to its stated total, with that total. rows: [agency code, fund, concept of expense, function, whole dollars per column]. Function and concept come from the draft crosswalk (dictionary_src/spending_crosswalk.csv, decision 76).

review.note: State budget figures, not federal grant work, but the budget's federal funds include HUD CDBG-DR and FEMA money, and the function crosswalk was reviewed on 2026-11-09 (decision 92). Decision 73 (7): leadership approved the Gasto Público page on 2026-11-09; the Compliance hold on federal grant content (decision 21) stays.

summary.en: Sector classification reviewed 2026-11-09; Compliance review of federal grant content open.
summary.es: Clasificación por sector revisada el 2026-11-09; revisión de Cumplimiento del contenido de subvenciones federales abierta.

title.en: Capital projects by municipio: the Planning Board's four-year investment program (PICA), by agency and fiscal year
title.es: Proyectos de mejoras capitales por municipio: el Programa de Inversiones de Cuatro Años (PICA) de la Junta de Planificación, por agencia y año fiscal

datasets.note: Federal funds returned and unused, decision 110 step 2 (taken_back.py). USAspending transaction search, every transaction on grants (award types 02 to 05) with place of performance Puerto Rico by action date from federal fiscal year 2019. For each award the transactions of one day count as one change, and the net reduction is the highest level its obligation reached in the period minus its final level; awards under $1,000 are left out. A reduction matched by an equal increase on another award of the same listing and agency within 31 days is a move and is not counted (read_counts.moves). totals: awards with a net reduction and their dollars; agencies: [awarding federal agency, awards, net reduction]; listings: [assistance listing, name, agency, awards, net reduction, awards that carry several listings]; by_year: [federal fiscal year of the award's last reduction, awards, net reduction]; apart: programs paid by actual cost, highway projects and disaster programs, each with its reason, never added to the totals. No recipient is read. The data do not say why an award was reduced.

title.en: Traffic on the main roads: arterials and major collectors with a count, annual average daily traffic (FHWA HPMS), map layer
title.es: Tránsito en las carreteras principales: arterias y colectoras principales con conteo, tránsito promedio diario anual (HPMS de la FHWA), capa del mapa

datasets.note: One line per stretch (3,829, 5,396.1 km): c (colour class 1-6 by vehicles a day), a (annual average daily traffic), r (route), f (functional class 1-5), y (year of the count), l (through lanes), km, t (trucks, % of vehicles, where reported), s (speed limit, mph), o (one direction of a divided road). Consecutive sections with the same count joined; lines simplified to 12 m. Drawn by the 2D map and the 3D view from core/facilities.js on first use (layer traffic). Built by traffic.py.

title.en: Road deaths by municipio and year: fatal crashes, people killed, pedestrians and bicyclists, motorcyclists, deaths per 100,000 residents and per 100 million vehicle-km (NHTSA FARS), counts only
title.es: Muertes en las carreteras por municipio y año: choques fatales, personas muertas, peatones y ciclistas, motociclistas, muertes por cada 100,000 residentes y por cada 100 millones de vehículo-km (FARS de la NHTSA), solo conteos

datasets.note: Six variables for the 78 municipios and Puerto Rico (geo.ids, the last is 72): crash_deaths, crash_fatal, crash_walk_bike and crash_moto for 2020-2024; crash_rate_5y and crash_per_vkm for 2020-2024 (under the year 2024). Counts only: no crash's place, date or time. 2024 is NHTSA's first release. Island totals since 2015 in notes.island. Built by crashes.py; docs/road-safety.md.
